items.title: Spotify Reveals Massive Spike in Streams for Music Featured in GTA 6
items.description: Spotify has released new data that shows huge spikes in streams for music featured in GTA 6, including a Carly Rae Jepsen song from over a decade ago.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Spotify has released new data that shows huge spikes in streams for music featured in GTA 6, including a Carly Rae Jepsen song from over a decade ago.

In an email sent to IGN, Spotify revealed that the GTA 6 hype is inspiring listeners to add tons of music from the game to their playlists. In addition to hype for the original music created specifically for the game, such as Justice's Flower in a Hurricane, Carly Rae Jepsen's 2015 song Run Away With Me saw a 940% increase in streams following the game's release. The song plays during a pivotal moment in GTA 6's first chapter and is arguably one of the best sections in the game.

Additionally, fans are listening to the official GTA 6 playlist en masse and are actively searching for things related to the game. You can view the full breakdown courtesy of Spotify below.

  • Following the release of GTA 6, streams of Carly Rae Jepsen's “Run Away With Me” spiked on Nov. 24, increasing by 940% in the U.S. and 1,255% in Canada compared to its average streams.
  • On Nov. 23, “Flower In A Hurricane” by Justice, Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard hit number 1 on BOTH Spotify’s Daily Top Songs charts globally and in the U.S.
  • Streams of The Official Grand Theft Auto Playlist surged week over week, rising 275% globally and 355% in the U.S. (on Nov. 19 as compared to Nov. 12).
  • GTA had fans searching for more. Searches containing “GTA,” “GTA6/VI” or “Grand Theft Auto” surged about 510% globally and 600% in the U.S. compared with the week prior (Nov. 19 vs. Nov. 12).

GTA 6 has been shattering all kinds of records and setting new trends. The game had the biggest launch in the history of PlayStation and sold nearly $4 billion worth of copies in its first 24 hours, making it the highest-grossing entertainment launch of all time by a significant margin. The game has also set viewership records on platforms like Twitch, led to a massive increase in internet traffic, and so much more.

It's a massive cultural moment that's likely not going to end anytime soon. Not only will this game likely get bigger, but it also has more big events on the horizon. It's also expected to release on PC early next year, and an online mode is also heavily speculated to come in the future.

items.title: Sunrise on the Reaping Director Reveals That Every Hunger Games Movie Has Initially Been Rated R
items.description: Longtime director of The Hunger Games franchise Francis Lawrence has revealed that all five films he has directed in the series were initially rated R and opened up about the process of making them PG-13.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Longtime director of The Hunger Games franchise Francis Lawrence has revealed that all five films he directed in the series were initially rated R, prompting clever workarounds when editing them.

On paper, The Hunger Games franchise is tonally very interesting. Although it's a young adult novel series, targeting teenagers, it's about children being forced to fight to the death in a dystopian society. The books don't hold back on the violence, and the films have always had to walk a fine line so they can reach the widest audience possible. The process of making the movies PG-13 is complicated and often inconsistent.

When speaking with Kevin McCarthy, director Francis Lawrence noted that all five of the Hunger Games films he has worked on were initially rated R. The director noted that across his whole career, he has run into an issue of making a movie with a PG-13 rating in mind, but the MPA (Motion Picture Association) reserves the right to give it an R if it's too "intense," even if there's no excessive blood, gore, language, or nudity. It happened with Constantine, it was a concern with I Am Legend, and it has happened regularly with The Hunger Games series.

In one of the Mockingjay films, Lawrence had to cut a scene of a little girl crying and screaming over the body of her dead mother. There wasn't any blood, but the performance was so visceral that it pushed the film closer to an R-rating.

He revealed that the process is somewhat subjective, as the people who rate the movies change, their tastes change, and he was even able to identify specific changes on particular movies.

In regards to Sunrise on the Reaping, he believes that the MPA has become more "conservative" with their judgment of a film, prompting them to tweak the project and show it to the organization four or five times. He also said that sometimes he makes the content more intense on purpose when presenting it to the MPA, so when they edit it, they can show the "intended" version, and it looks more tame by comparison. One example of this is amplifying sound effects to make it sound gnarlier, and then reigning it in on subsequent edits.

Lawrence went on to note that he is surprised by how much these movies can get away with in a PG-13 context, but believes there's a thematic relevance that the MPA accepts.

"It does help that there's been so many of these now that there's [a] precedent," he said. "There's also real thematic relevance to these stories, and I think that also really helps, that in the end they're anti-violence stories. They're about the consequences of violence, the consequences of war; they're really about themes that are educating people. I do think the MPA takes that into consideration when they look at sequences that are intense. They have different emotional values, and it's not really splattercore, in a way.

"But I definitely do intensify beyond a limit of where I think it will be accepted as PG-13 purposely, because I know we are going to have to pull back on certain things."

He explained that certain deaths were more brutal and gratuitous in initial cuts of the film, but ultimately had to be adjusted for a PG-13 rating.

"One thing I really wanted to keep was we had a very specific neck wound on Maysilee in her death. Basically the one that kills her is right here," said Lawrence while pointing at the center of his neck. "And he's covering it and when his hand comes off, you can see blood starting to drip out of it, and you can see the hole, and it's why she can't speak. And they made us get rid of that, and that's what killed me."

The Hunger Games films are far from the only big mainstream action movies that have to get creative with how they depict violence. Crew members on The Dark Knight were confident the film would be rated R, despite Christopher Nolan and the studio working to avoid that. They were able to get around a harder rating thanks to the fact the film does most of the gorier acts of violence off-screen or even playing it off as a joke.

"It’s kind of shocking that The Dark Knight ended up being PG-13," said the film's cinematographer Wally Pfister in a 2018 interview. "All of Chris’s movies would be PG-13 to open it up to a wider audience. Somehow, he always had some magic with the MPA.

"Lo and behold, he has the pencil and I’m like, 'You are not getting the PG-13 with that. There’s no way this is going in. He’s driving this pencil through a guy’s head!' And I was wrong. Chris was always right, whether you liked it or not. You’d be like, 'F*** you, you were right again.' With this pencil trick, I thought, ‘If it has the right amount of levity, we’ll sell this and it won’t come off as being violent but it’ll come off as being a magic trick and it’ll come off as being a punchline.’ And it was!"

Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters now.

items.title: GTA 6 Animation Director Reveals Rockstar Made 3 Animations for Each Item Interaction
items.description: Mike Jones, the director of gameplay animation for GTA 6, revealed that the team at Rockstar created three separate animations for each item interaction in the game.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Mike Jones, the director of gameplay animation for GTA 6, revealed that the team at Rockstar created three separate animations for each item interaction in the game.

If you’ve been playing GTA 6 at all, you’ve probably picked up on the fact that characters can now hold an item in each hand. This has made for some especially funny clips on social media, where users have wasted no time making Jason recreate the ‘six-seven’ meme while holding various objects.

This is a big change from previous Rockstar games; in titles like GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, players could only carry one thing at a time, though you could dual wield certain guns in GTA: San Andreas. (You could also hold longarms at your side while shooting a pistol in RDR 2 and Max Payne 3.) Now, you can hold a sandwich in one hand and a drink in the other — or a bag and a gun, if you’re sticking up a pawn shop, for instance. This isn’t just an aesthetic feature, either, as it serves the important function of letting players take care of two tasks at once, making robberies or transporting items a bit smoother.

Players have praised GTA 6 for its jaw-dropping attention to detail, and this particular tidbit wasn’t lost on them. A thread on Bluesky discussing the feature caught the attention of Mike Jones, the director of gameplay on Rockstar’s latest title, who revealed the extent of the studio’s efforts in making sure every single item interaction had a single-handed, two-handed, and hands-free animations.

“FYI, we made three versions for all item interactions; one if both hands are free, one if just your right hand is free and again for the left,” he wrote. “It was a massive pain, but once you knew every interaction could ‘cope,’ it made the game logic much easier. That was then sometimes replicated for crouch, too…”

That being said, the devs at Rockstar aren’t superheroes, and they had to cut corners somewhere during development. Jones admitted this fact in response to another comment in this thread, where a user wrote, “Honestly, the level of polish is so absurd that when I see how cheated the ‘putting gas in the car’ sequence is, I'm like, relieved. ‘Oh, okay, they're human, they bleed.’ You all did SO well.”

“Thanks, everyone would really appreciate your comments! And yes, shortcuts were definitely made, too,” Jones replied.

GTA 6 is a game like no other. Its world is so massive and detailed that some players are avoiding progressing the story in favor of chilling out in Key Lento and diving for treasure, fishing with Cal, and playing billiards at the Rusty Anchor. And we can’t blame them; there’s tons of stuff to do, even in Chapter 1.

items.title: LEGO Announces 4 New Sets Based on the Harry Potter HBO Series
items.author: Chris Reed
items.content:
The LEGO Harry Potter theme has been a mainstay since the first set came out in 2001. Now that HBO has a new TV adaptation of the Wizarding World in the works (set to debut on December 25), LEGO has finally unveiled a new batch of sets based on the new series. Four new sets have been announced, two of which are available to preorder now. They're all out January 1. Let’s take a look.

Featured in this article

The four sets offer a nice selection of characters and locations from the first book, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone, which is what the HBO show’s first season adapts.

Honestly, these sets don’t look all that distinct from the sets based on the movies. Then again, based on the TV show’s trailer, they didn’t really change much when adapting the franchise into a show.

LEGO Harry Potter: Privet Drive

  • Preorder at LEGO

It all starts on 4 Privet Drive. That’s where we find the home of the Dursley family, who adopt Harry Potter after you-know-who kills his parents. The Dursleys aren’t very nice to Harry, but this LEGO set lets you build their two-story house, complete with Harry’s cupboard under the stairs. This one’s available for preorder now.

LEGO Harry Potter: Gryffindor Common Room

  • Preorder at LEGO

The three main young wizards all end up in house Gryffindor, so they spend a lot of time in the common room. This set recreates that cozy space, complete with a fireplace, five minifigures, and a Quidditch table that’s unique to the show.

LEGO Harry Potter: Hogwarts Express & Platform 9¾

  • Not available for preorder

There are so many now-iconic things in the first book that it must have been hard to pick what to base sets on. That said, it would be a shame if there wasn’t a new Hogwarts Express set. This set has platform 9¾, plus the bold red train. It also includes minifigures for Harry, Hermione, Ron, Draco Malfoy, and Molly Weasley — all characters that appear in or around the train in the book.

LEGO BrickHeadz: Harry, Draco and Hagrid Figures

  • Not available for preorder

BrickHeadz are kind of like LEGO’s take on Funko Pops. They depict known characters from pop culture, but in a stylized design, and they’re meant for display. These seem like good, blocky renditions of the trio they depict.

For more, check out all the best LEGO Black Friday deals available now. And take a gander at our running list of every upcoming LEGO set announced so far.

items.title: 'People Are Doing It Too Quickly Now' — The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Director Speaks Out on YA Franchise Reboots
items.description: I got the chance to sit down with the director of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Francis Lawrence, who opened up about the amount of remakes happening in Hollywood and how he would feel if The Hunger Games series ever got rebooted.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
I got the chance to sit down with the director of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Francis Lawrence, who opened up about the amount of remakes happening in Hollywood and how he would feel if The Hunger Games series ever got rebooted.

Francis Lawrence has directed all but one movie in The Hunger Games series. He’s been with the franchise for over a decade; the first film, directed by Gary Ross, released in 2012, after which Lawrence took up the mantle for all subsequent movies.

It’s one of several iconic movie franchises that defined the YA boom of the 2000s - mid-2010s. And unlike other series from this time period, it has neither languished nor suffered a reboot before its corpse is even cold.

HBO’s forthcoming Harry Potter series is perhaps the most egregious example of such a reboot. The last Harry Potter movie released in 2011, and its cast defined an entire generation of fans who grew up watching their adventures at Hogwarts. It seems almost insulting to reimagine the world that was so painstakingly built over the course of a decade — but that’s just my opinion.

I’m not alone in this line of thinking, though. When asked about his feelings on reboots, Lawrence agreed that they’re happening too soon, bringing up Warner Bros.’ thankfully canceled idea for an I Am Legend reboot in 2014, just seven years after the original film was released.

“I mean, I do feel like people are doing it sort of too quickly now,” he mused. “I agree with you on that. People started talking about that with I Am Legend. I don't remember how long ago, but it felt like 10 years had gone by or something, and somebody was thinking of remaking it already at Warner. I'm like, ‘Really? 10 years, that's it?’”

Given the imminent release of HBO’s Harry Potter series on Christmas day, I had to bring up the very real possibility that The Hunger Games sees a reboot in the next decade or so — an idea that Lawrence wasn’t sure would get Suzanne Collins’ blessing.

“I don't know how I would feel about it,” he admitted. “I also don't know if Suzanne has anything in place to sort of protect against that, but that'd be really, really interesting to figure out. But I think it's a tough one. I mean, if Suzanne backed it, I think some spinoffs, and obviously if she writes other books, things like that could be interesting, as long as she backs it and comes up with it and has the thematic reasonings and philosophies that she usually does, that would be cool. But I don't know how you go back and remake the original movies and it not be [Jennifer Lawrence]."

To his point, The Hunger Games franchise has managed to stay in the public consciousness, owing in part to its later release during the YA boom (the final film in the original series came out in 2015) and its two prequel movies that rocked theaters in the 2020s. The latest movie, Sunrise on the Reaping, received solid reviews from critics, earning an 8 out of 10 from IGN.

For more news on this newest entry in The Hunger Games series, check out my interview with star Joseph Zada, who told me all about how he managed to pull off Woody Harrelson's unmistakable accent, and whether or not the cast is Team Peeta or Team Gale.

Given the imminent release of HBO’s Harry Potter series on Christmas day, I had to bring up the very real possibility that The Hunger Games sees a reboot in the next decade or so — an idea that Lawrence wasn’t sure would get Suzanne Collins’ blessing.

items.title: GTA 6 Doesn't Let You Replay Missions, and Rockstar Says There's a Good Reason for That
items.description: GTA 6 gives players a lot of freedom in how the story and quests play out, but it came at the cost of letting players replay missions, according to Rockstar.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
GTA 6 gives players a lot of freedom in how the story and quests play out, but it came at the cost of letting players replay missions, according to Rockstar.

When speaking with Kotaku, Rockstar Games senior design director Scott Butchard explained why the studio scrapped a mission replay menu in GTA 6. Both GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 allowed players to freely replay missions, but that's not the case in GTA 6. According to Butchard, they considered bringing the feature back, but cut it because it was "at odds" with the story.

“Mission replay was certainly something we looked at early on in development, and we do not currently support it,” said Butchard. “As the game came together it felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected. Sitting outside of the game as it were and replaying missions really diminished the choices you had made.”

The lack of a mission replay option has been a point of contention for fans. GTA 6 has some of the best missions in the franchise, particularly the final mission of Chapter 1. Given that GTA 6 can take players anywhere from 50 - 100 hours to finish, most people probably won't start the entire game over just to re-experience their favorite mission. However, it's worth noting that Butchard says the game doesn't "currently support" this feature. Maybe it'll come in the form of an update later, but Rockstar hasn't confirmed that.

GTA 6's story and missions can deviate somewhat significantly based on your choices. Certain characters can be killed or spared, objectives can be completed in different ways, and the entire relationship between Jason and Lucia can vary based on your actions. You can get entirely different dialogue options and cutscenes based on these differences, which might be why a mission replay system isn't as straightforward as it was previous games.

However, Red Dead Redemption 2 also featured different choices that changed Arthur's character. It wasn't quite as nuanced as GTA 6's variations, though. Maybe Rockstar will figure out a way to do this, but it clearly fell low on the priority list, if it was on the list at all by the end of development. Even if Rockstar never adds it, modders will probably find a way to slot it in when the inevitable PC version releases.

items.title: 'It Would Be Absolutely Incredible' — Hideki Kamiya Wants to Make a New Castlevania Game With Konami
items.description: Hideki Kamiya, the mind behind Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and Okami, wants to make a new Castlevania game, saying his team at CLOVERS could make something “absolutely incredible.”
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Hideki Kamiya, the mind behind Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and Okami, wants to make a new Castlevania game, saying his team at CLOVERS could make something "absolutely incredible" alongside Konami.

Hideki Kamiya is back in the saddle at CLOVERS, his independent game studio made up of former CLOVER staff who are currently hard at work on the Okami sequel. He made the company’s independent status extremely clear in his latest YouTube video, reminding excited fans to stop asking him about Capcom-owned franchises (or even sequels to games like God Hand, since he had no part in its development).

Given CLOVERS’ status as an independent company that’s already working with a major developer in Capcom, Kamiya floated ideas for future collaborations with other big developers once the Okami sequel is out in the world. One of those ideas was a partnership with Konami for a Castlevania game, which he promised would be “incredible,” if it actually ends up happening.

“Since we’re independent and don’t have any outside funding, we want to stay on good terms — or rather, collaborate — with various companies and keep doing interesting things,” he explained. “Of course, I want to keep building a good relationship with Capcom, and naturally, I’d like to be on good terms with Nintendo, too.

“...Maybe I could make a new Getsufumaden with Konami. Oh, and Castlevania. If we made it, it would be absolutely incredible, so please, let us take the job. I am a bit busy right now, though,” he laughed.

A Castlevania game from a mind like Kamiya’s would definitely be something special. Would it be a 3D action game like Bayonetta, or more of a 2D side-scroller in the vein of Viewtiful Joe? The possibilities are endless, and given that Konami is already on a mission to revitalize its classic IPs with new games, the possibility of a team-up with CLOVERS on a Castlevania title isn’t totally out of the question.

It's also worth noting that the Castlevania franchise enjoyed a new installment in Belmont's Curse late last month. Alongside its animated adaptations on Netflix, Konami's classic vampire-slaying game series is getting a second wind, and Kamiya would like to be part of that, though whether or not this actually happens remains to be seen.

Kamiya also brought up ideas for other potential games that CLOVERS might make in collaboration with big publishers in the future, though how serious he was about these is up to interpretation. He playfully mentioned making a Star Fox sequel with Koei Tecmo or a King’s Knight sequel with Square Enix, and even mentioned a Kinnikuman M.U.S.C.L.E.: Tag Team Match game with Bandai Namco. Of course, these are all just goofy ideas he likely said in jest, but it does seem like he’s eager to make more games with major companies once Okami is out the door.

The Okami sequel was first announced at the 2024 Game Awards. It’s only been two years since then, so it’s unlikely that we’ll hear anything else from CLOVERS about the game’s development process anytime soon. However, you can read our exclusive interview with Kamiya, done just after the sequel’s TGA announcement, or check out our chat with him from the Lucca Comics & Games Festival just last month.

items.title: Sony Confirms PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for December 2026
items.description: Sony has confirmed the PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for December, which will be available to download from Tuesday, December 1 to Monday January 4.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Sony has confirmed the PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for December, which will be available to download from Tuesday, December 1 to Monday January 4.

In a PlayStation Blog post, Sony said Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, and Amnesia: The Bunker are December’s three titles. Will you be able to tear yourself away from GTA 6 to give either of these games a shot? Or perhaps you're after a palate cleanser after pumping 100 hours into Rockstar's epic?

IGN's Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 + 4 review returned an 8/10. We said: "Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 + 4 proves yet again the series’ over-the-top skateboarding formula is totally timeless, even if some of the changes to THPS4 miss the mark and the soundtrack has been fumbled."

Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, meanwhile, got a 7.5 back in 2017. "Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 is an ambitious , if rough-edged experience, with deceptively deep RPG and brawling elements," we said at the time.

And our Amnesia: The Bunker review returned an 8. We said: "Amnesia: The Bunker is a smaller, more self-contained episode in the groundbreaking horror franchise that shows Frictional still has some chilling new tricks up their sleeves."

PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for December 2026

  • Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4 – Cross-Gen Edition | PS5, PS4
  • Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 | PS5, PS4
  • Amnesia: The Bunker | PS4

It’s worth noting that PlayStation Plus members have until Monday, November 30 to add the PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for November (Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider IV – VI Remastered, Monster Train 2) to their library.

items.title: One of GTA 6's Best Features Was Actually Planned for GTA: Vice City, Reveals Ex-Rockstar Dev
items.description: GTA 6's headphones mechanic was originally planned to be included in the original GTA: Vice City, according to a former Rockstar Games employee.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
GTA 6's headphones mechanic was originally planned to be included in the original GTA: Vice City, according to a former Rockstar Games employee.

Ex-Rockstar Games dev Obbe Vermeji revealed that the headphones feature was cut from GTA: Vice City due to a technical reason, and they had even created an icon for it. It's unclear what the technical reason was, but Vice City's version likely would've come in the form of a Walkman or cassette player, given it was set in the 80s. GTA 6's version, however, comes with a smartphone and a pair of AirPods.

The feature is pretty incredible, because you can listen to music and podcasts wherever you go. You no longer have to sit in the car to finish a song; you can just get out, put your headphones in, and turn on the radio station you were just listening to. And when combined with combat encounters, it can have some thrilling results. Last night, In the Air Tonight came on as I approached a gang hideout, creating an incredibly cinematic moment for me.

This is the best game ever made dude https://t.co/AFR2jmo0fF

— Cade Onder (@Cade_Onder) November 25, 2026

It doesn't always have to lead to some epic moment, though. It's great for working out in-game, learning about the world and lore of GTA via podcasts and talk shows, and much more. A lot of effort has been packed into creating GTA 6's in-game media, and the headphones allow you to make full use of it. The only downside is that you can't make any kind of custom playlists. Presumably, this is because Rockstar wants players to organically discover music from the radio stations instead of curating the songs they already know and love.

The option would be nice, but personally, there are so many great songs I may have never heard if GTA's radio stations didn't expose me to them. Maybe a future update or the inevitable online mode will include a playlist option, but it could be a while before we see such a thing.

items.title: GTA 6: Breaking Down The Cleanest Bank Robbery We've Seen So Far
items.description: One GTA 6 player has robbed $160,000 in just one minute in the cleanest bank robbery we’ve seen yet. Here's how they did it.
items.author: Simon Cardy
items.content:
Warning: This article talks about gameplay mechanics from chapter four of GTA 6, but contains no story spoilers.

GTA 6 is a game all about making money. One of the quickest and most profitable ways of doing that is by robbing one of Vice City’s biggest banks. It’s also one of the riskiest, though; we’ve a legion of law enforcement destined to descend upon you once that alarm is triggered. That doesn’t mean a clean escape isn’t possible, though, and that’s just what one streamer has showcased, in perhaps the most impressive manner we’ve seen so far.

Video game streamer Sway set about his mission to the downtown Lombank for all its worth via a popular method – tailing a security van. These are the green and white vans you sometimes see driving around the map, which, if you follow for long enough, will lead you to a bank where the vault will be left wide open for you to enter. You can also make the locations of these trucks visible by paying Yasmani a hefty $10,000 tip for the info.

It’s worth noting that this option isn’t available until chapter four, with banks not being able to be successfully robbed at all until partway through GTA 6’s third chapter, once you gain the ability to cash in on marked bills. Otherwise, you’ll end up as Lucia can in the prologue, with a whole load of coloured dye all over you.

Anyway, back to Sway’s attempted heist, and just because the security guard has opened the vault doesn’t mean you can simply walk in and out of the building carrying a load of cash. There are numerous options you can take, including blasting your way in and getting in and out as quickly and violently as possible, or entering through the back rooms to sneak past everyone. The latter is the way that Sway mostly went with.

First, he shot out a security camera in the rear alley with a silenced pistol, before cracking open a garage door and quickly knocking out a guard with a quick pistol whip. Another couple of security members fell unconscious thanks to the blunt end of a gun as he made his way swiftly into the vault. Just noting the excellent choice of “old person” mask from Jason here, too.

Cleanest Bank Robbery you'll see in GTA 6.

$150k in 1 minute.
simple and clean. https://t.co/Y8GqDuydvd

— sway (@swaywtw) November 25, 2026

Next come the stacks of marked bills, which are hurriedly bundled into stash bags by Lucia. This action triggers the bank’s alarm systems, and always will, as far as I know. The cloud-based security camera system can’t be overrun and will always alert the cops once a couple of bundles of notes hit the bottom of your bag. With $122,000 already secured, he smartly swaps to controlling Jason, who can fill up his own bag to maximise the profits. With the grand total now sitting at $160,000, the hard part begins. At least, in theory, it should be difficult.

This clearly isn’t Sway’s first run, though, as he doesn’t panic at all. He runs back to where he entered from, kneecapping an onrushing guard with a single bullet before reopening the garage door to exit the bank and remove the couple’s masks, in turn removing the appearance marker from the top right. Cleverly, Lucia’s personal vehicle — a sleek sports car, yet another sign this isn’t his first heist if he can afford to register that — is sitting just feet away. He changes into a fresh pair of clothes, holsters his weapon, and just like that, becomes completely incognito. Little do the cops who have just rolled up know that the people walking past them are exactly who they’re at the bank for, and he simply walks across the road and out of the red circle on the minimap towards freedom.

It’s an incredibly quick, clean in-and-out operation, and the sort of robbery that feels extra satisfying to pull off in GTA 6. It’s the kind of hidden-in-plain-sight thrill that you’d expect from the likes of the Hitman series, but pulled off in a dynamic open world that loves to throw surprises your way. There’s no “correct” method, either. It can be just as fun to barrel through the main doors of a Fleeca and set a series of sticky bomb charges to gain access to the cash behind locked doors and inside safes. The huge-scale chases that can develop from botched escapes deliver a thrill, too, with chaos often reigning supreme.

Literally, as I've been writing this, Sway himself has released a video showcasing how you can rob all eight of Leonida's biggest banks in as quick and clean a way as possible.

How to Rob ALL 8 Major Banks CLEAN.

$125k - $200k Each Bank.
All in Under 2 mins Each. https://t.co/iqtFplFof7

— sway (@swaywtw) November 25, 2026

I, like I assume many of you, have spent a lot of time on social media the past few days watching what other players have been getting up to in GTA 6. There’s a fantastic range out there from smooth scenes like this one to more creative attempts — only this morning did I see someone fill up their car with stash bags, but because the police had identified the vehicle, they instead chose to drive a tow truck and drag their original car around the city with them, thus fooling the cops.

What have been some of your favourite robbery methods in GTA 6? Let us know in the comments.

items.title: The Witcher 3 and Assassin's Creed 'Reset Player Expectations' for Open-World Action RPGs, So the Fable Reboot Devs Had to Look Beyond the Original Trilogy for Inspiration
items.description: Why has the Fable reboot taken so long to develop? There are a number of reasons, but part of it is that expectations around open-world action RPGs were reset by various competing games over the past decade.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Why has the Fable reboot taken so long to develop? There are a number of reasons, but part of it is that expectations around open-world action RPGs were reset by various competing games over the past decade.

Work on Fable reportedly started in 2016, and only now, 10 years later, is it near release. It’s suffered a tumultuous development but, unlike some other costly Microsoft gaming projects, it has avoided closure amid sweeping layoffs and restructuring at Xbox.

In a new interview with GamesIndustry.biz, Playground Games co-founder and Fable general manager Ralph Fulton touched on the trials and tribulations Fable has endured over the years. Playground set up a new team to make Fable in addition to its hugely popular racing game franchise, Forza Horizon, and set out to make a game in a genre it had no prior experience with. And Fable is a big role-playing game, with all the bells and whistles you'd expect. So, Fable isn’t technically a debut game from Playground, but it sort of is.

In terms of what’s changed, Fulton said that technology had “advanced” during development, pointing to a reset of player expectations with the release of CD Projekt’s fantasy RPG masterpiece The Witcher 3 and then Assassin’s Creed’s move towards the RPG genre.

This, Fulton explained, meant that Playground had to look beyond the original Fable trilogy for inspiration to ensure it created a reboot that would meet modern open-world standards.

“In 2015, The Witcher 3 redefined what an open-world action RPG looks like and became the gold standard,” Fulton explained. “And after that bar was raised, the Assassin's Creed franchise changed into this more modern iteration with Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla, and became like a quasi-RPG.

“All of these games continue to reset player expectations, which means I think looking only to the original Fable trilogy for inspiration would leave us lacking in terms of what the modern audience, the modern marketplace, expects.”

Despite this, the scope of Fable actually decreased over time, with the project starting with “an enormous potential scope.” In August, Playground confirmed that Fable’s main quest will take around 20 hours to beat, with an additional 15-20 hours of side and open-world exploration content available. Howlongtobeat has the original 2004 Fable's main quest clocking in at about 12-and-a-half hours. Fable 2 isn't much longer at 13 hours, and Fable 3 inches just further past that at 13-and-a-half hours. So, the Fable reboot is shaping up to be the longest in the series.

Fable is set for launch on February 23, 2027, across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X and S.

items.title: Blade Runner 2099 Showrunner Explains the References to Philip K. Dick's Novel, Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep
items.description: Silka Luisa, the creator, executive producer, and showrunner of Blade Runner 2099, explained why this series was the first entry in the franchise to include certain references from Philip K. Dick’s original novel.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Silka Luisa, the creator, executive producer, and showrunner of Blade Runner 2099, recently explained to IGN why this series was the first entry in the franchise to include certain references to Philip K. Dick’s original novel.

Warning: MAJOR spoilers for Blade Runner 2099 ahead! Turn back now if you haven’t watched the show!

Philip K. Dick’s genre-defining sci-fi novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? is the basis upon which Ridley Scott built the first Blade Runner movie back in 1982. It certainly had its differences from the source material — though Dick himself praised a television preview he saw just before his death — and was notably lacking a few central elements from the book, chief among them the empathy box and Deckard’s hand-wringing over a vanity purchase of an actual, real-life animal (hence the book’s title).

Near the beginning of the book, Deckard is in knots about keeping up with the Joneses; in the novel’s post-war future where global conditions have been extremely averse to almost all forms of life, animals are a rarity, and owning one is a luxury. Deckard and his wife — to whom he appears to harbor relative indifference, if not annoyance — own an electric sheep, which they keep on the rooftop of their apartment building.

Unable to stand the constraints of his financial class, he decides to purchase a black Nubian goat, which he hesitantly shows to his wife, who predictably blows up at him for making such a massive purchase without consulting her. She eventually comes around to the animal after actually setting eyes on it, however. (Eventually, the goat is killed by Rachael, a replicant with whom Deckard has an affair.) While this specific storyline isn’t in the original movie nor any subsequent Blade Runner media, a black goat does appear in Silka’s show.

This goat makes its appearance on the sea cliffs near Cora and Elias’s childhood home, which is where they lived with their adoptive mother, Helena. As Cora later comes to discover, Helena was one of the very first replicants ever made, a Nexus 1, created without a set lifespan and essentially immortal (as long as they can void injury or accidents). It’s a lovely parallel with the book as the goat represented Deckard’s desperation to cling to his humanity and his status in society. Helena was also a way for Cora to cling to her own humanity in a world run by replicants. But after learning that her mother was a Nexus 1, this illusion crashes down on her, much like the goat after it was pushed off the roof of Deckard’s apartment building by his scorned replicant lover.

Also included for the first time is the empathy box, a technological marvel that allows users to mentally and physically "feel" the events of whatever they are seeing on a screen in front of them. In this case, it’s Wilbur Mercer, a religious figure whose laborious climb up a mountain while being pelted with rocks has become a central part of a religion aptly named "Mercerism." In the book, the footage is discovered to be fake, having been filmed on a sound stage; Mercer was merely a character played by an actor named Al Jarry.

The empathy box shows up in one of the final episodes of Blade Runner 2099. A Mercerite forces the dying replicant Olwen to use the box, where she watches Mercer climb the mountain and feels herself being pelted with stones.

I asked Silka about these references and why she felt they were important to include in the show when previous adaptations had largely ignored them in favor of building upon Scott’s specific version of Dick’s literary world.

“I mean, Philip K. Dick is a genius,” Silka told me. “His book is so prescient. I think what's so special about him and his writing is not just that he was able to look into the future and really see not only what would happen, but the dangers of what would happen, but he also has a way of doing it where it's this playful, zany tone that you almost... It doesn't leave you with a feeling of dread, but the ideas are very, very dark. And the juxtaposition of those two things, this playful tone plus these dark ideas, that felt like a direction and a north star, tonally, for us to pursue.

“And also just as a lover of the book, I love Mercerism. I was so curious as to, ‘Okay, what would an empathy box look like? Who were the practitioners? What did Wilbur's climb actually look like?’ So much of that had lived in my imagination. And so then, to be able to actually sit with people and say, ‘Well, what do you think it looks like?’ And then look at references and build that out, it was really exciting."

I mentioned to Silka that I had paused the show to check my own copy of the book, just to make sure I wasn’t hallucinating that I remembered something about a guy climbing a mountain and getting hit with a bunch of rocks. It actually made me re-read the novel, which, in turn, gave me a much greater appreciation for the series. (Silka also mentioned that the show boasts a few additional references to Dick’s short stories; a girl’s toy robot named "My Lord" is one of these.)

“That’s what I hope [happens],” an enthusiastic Silka replied. “Everyone should read it.”

Blade Runner 2099 is available to steam on Prime Video. For more news about the show, check out my interview with Alcon Entertainment co-CEOs Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, as well as IGN’s review of this latest entry in the Blade Runner franchise.

items.title: 'It's Such a Shame' — Blade Runner 2099's Lewis Gribben Mourns EA's Closure of BioWare
items.description: I got the chance to sit down with the supporting cast of Blade Runner 2099, and naturally, we started chatting about video games. I had to ask about their favorite games, to which Lewis Gribben gave a topical answer involving the now-shuttered BioWare.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
I got the chance to sit down with the supporting cast of Blade Runner 2099, and naturally, we started chatting about video games. I had to ask about their favorite games, to which Lewis Gribben gave a topical answer involving the now-shuttered BioWare.

BioWare — the Canadian game studio behind hit AAA RPGs like Dragon Age and Mass Effect — was closed by EA in October, sparking outrage among fans and those within the industry itself. The knife twisted further when a former BioWare employee leaked a trailer for the next Mass Effect game, which, by all accounts, looked extremely ambitious and well in the middle of production. (EA decided to cancel the project rather than move it to a different development team or sell it off to another studio.)

Lewis Gribben, who plays Elias opposite Hunter Schafer’s Cora in Blade Runner 2099, gushed about the Mass Effect series and mourned the loss of BioWare, while also making sure to float his name for a possible role in Amazon’s TV adaptation of the games.

“There’s so many [games] that I could mention, but the franchise that I think is one of the best sci-fi franchises is Mass Effect,” Gribben told me. “I think it’s so good. I think it’s such an amazing and incredible world. I know Amazon is considering making a TV show of it. Please, think about me for it.

“I think it’s so good, and I think it’s such a shame that BioWare shut down recently and that studio is no longer gonna exist, but they were so great at telling epic stories and you getting to choose how you shape your character, good or bad, and I think that adjacent to being a franchise and a sci-fi world is what makes the franchise so amazing.”

Dimitri Abold, who plays the character Bebeto, said his favorite game is Final Fantasy 7, and that he’s looking forward to the next installment in the remake trilogy next year. Matthew Needham, who plays the replicant named Yahya, revealed that he started playing video games during the pandemic with The Last of Us — which he joked was probably not the best pick during a global virus, though we all agreed that it was a standout game and a good choice for someone just getting into gaming.

Following up on this question, I revealed a tidbit from my conversation with Alcon Entertainment co-CEOs Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, who told me that they have had talks about adapting Blade Runner into a AAA video game. All three actors seemed excited by the idea and said they were game to be part of the project, if it ever comes to fruition.

“It would be really cool,” Gribben said. “We could kind of connect the TV show with the game.”

“That’d be so sick,” Abold remarked excitedly, to which Needham replied, “That’d be fun.”

Blade Runner 2099 is available to stream on Prime Video. For more news about the series, check out IGN’s review, as well as our explainer for its ending in case you had a few remaining questions after watching.

items.title: Fan-Made GTA 5 Port for iPhone Shuts Down After Take-Two Cease and Desist
items.description: A cease and desist from Rockstar parent company Take-Two has put an end to a fan-made port of GTA 5 for Apple devices a month after the creator went public with it.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
A cease and desist from Rockstar parent company Take-Two has put an end to a fan-made port of GTA 5 for Apple devices a month after the creator went public with it.

Five Star Port launched in October this year as a full native port that ran locally on iPhone, iPad, and Mac. On newer hardware like the A20 Pro chip, the port boasted frame rates between 40 and 60fps at near-native resolution and max graphics settings. It also supported foldable phones, with the controllers and map appearing on the lower portion and the game on the upper portion of the screen.

Kevin, the creator of the port, posted a farewell message to the unofficial port’s website. “GTA V has always been one of my favorite games,” he said. “I've made mods for it, worked with FiveM, managed and hosted FiveM servers, and played on plenty of others. It has given me a lot of great memories. Getting to bring it to people who don't have a PC or a console, so they could play it on a phone, has been really, really cool. I honestly never thought this game could run on a phone at all.

“Take-Two Interactive, through their lawyers, has sent me a cease and desist asking me to stop all activity under the Five Star Port name and everything related to it. I am complying with it.”

Five Star Port’s website, app, and online services were shut down immediately. The Telegram and Discord groups have been made read-only and will be deleted on November 27.

“I'm not involved in and don't endorse any continuation, rebrand or copy of the port, and I can't help with files or links,” Kevin added. He also posted a warning that scammers have been passing around copies of the port, claiming to have a “new version” of it. These could spread computer viruses.

“Thank you again to everyone who supported this project: everyone who playtested, everyone who sent suggestions and feedback, and everyone who helped make it a great port that is actually fully playable on an iPhone,” Kevin signed off. “That still feels wild to me.”

Take-Two has a history of forcing fan projects offline, so perhaps it comes as no surprise to see Five Star Port fall by the wayside. The company is currently battling homebrew efforts to vibecode a PC port of GTA 6, which some believe is mere days away from being playable.

items.title: Hollow Knight: Silksong Dev Gets Into the Direct Business With Cherry Time! Special Presentation
items.description: Team Cherry has announced an upcoming Cherry Time! Special Presentation, during which it will issue an update on the hotly anticipated Hollow Knight: Silksong expansion, Sea of Sorrow.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Team Cherry has announced an upcoming Cherry Time! Special Presentation, during which it will issue an update on the hotly anticipated Hollow Knight: Silksong expansion, Sea of Sorrow.

The Australian developer said this YouTube presentation will include “a bunch of exciting announcements” in addition to the Sea of Sorrow update, sparking speculation that the developer may be ready to discuss what’s next. There is also speculation around what the Sea of Sorrow update will be. Could it be a shadow drop? A release date announcement for before the end of the year? Or, perhaps, word that Sea of Sorrow is somehow three times as big as expected so it's delayed and now a full-on sequel? Roll the dice!

Cherry Time! Special Presentation is set for 7am PT / 10am ET / 3pm UK time on Friday, November 27.

Team Cherry teased the nautically themed Sea of Sorrow in December last year with a 2026 release window. It's free for all players. As part of the DLC announcement, Team Cherry said Hollow Knight: Silksong had sold more than 7 million copies since going on sale in September 2025, and had millions more playing on Xbox Game Pass.

"It’s a truly staggering number of players, more than we could have ever expected (enough to crash all of the storefronts!)," Team Cherry said at the time. "Watching the community grow, seeing the amazing art, the mods, the unexpected strategies, and the support between players through the game’s challenges has been hugely rewarding for us here at home. Your continued enthusiasm remains a massive motivator as we work towards expanding the game even further."

IGN's Hollow Knight: Silksong review scored the game 9/10. We said: "Hollow Knight: Silksong is packed full of sharp platforming, enticing exploration, and nail-biting combat that's all unapologetically challenging in just the right way."

The Australian developer said this YouTube presentation will include “a bunch of exciting announcements” in addition to the Sea of Sorrow update, sparking speculation that the developer may be ready to discuss what’s next. There is also speculation around what the Sea of Sorrow update will be. Could it be a shadow drop? A release date announcement for before the end of the year? Or, perhaps, word that Sea of Sorrow is somehow three times as big as expected so it's delayed and now a full-on sequel? Roll the dice!

Cherry Time! Special Presentation is set for 7am PT / 10am ET / 3pm UK time on Friday, November 27.

Team Cherry teased the nautically themed Sea of Sorrow in December last year with a 2026 release window. It's free for all players. As part of the DLC announcement, Team Cherry said Hollow Knight: Silksong had sold more than 7 million copies since going on sale in September 2025, and had millions more playing on Xbox Game Pass.

"It’s a truly staggering number of players, more than we could have ever expected (enough to crash all of the storefronts!)," Team Cherry said at the time. "Watching the community grow, seeing the amazing art, the mods, the unexpected strategies, and the support between players through the game’s challenges has been hugely rewarding for us here at home. Your continued enthusiasm remains a massive motivator as we work towards expanding the game even further."

IGN's Hollow Knight: Silksong review scored the game 9/10. We said: "Hollow Knight: Silksong is packed full of sharp platforming, enticing exploration, and nail-biting combat that's all unapologetically challenging in just the right way."

items.title: The Witcher 4 and All CD Projekt's Upcoming Games Remain Multiplatform Despite PlayStation Marketing Deal, CD Projekt Boss Reassures
items.description: CD Projekt co-CEO Michał Nowakowski has reassured fans that The Witcher 4 remains a multiplatform game despite its PlayStation marketing deal with Sony.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
CD Projekt co-CEO Michał Nowakowski has reassured fans that The Witcher 4 remains a multiplatform game despite its PlayStation marketing deal with Sony.

Announced yesterday as part of CD Projekt’s latest financial results, the partnership with Sony Interactive Entertainment also covers its games on PlayStation and PlayStation Plus. CD Projekt said the deal “will support our business and financial outlook in this and future years.”

While the terms of the deal remain undisclosed, it is expected that The Witcher 4 marketing will feature PS5 prominently, perhaps even exclusively, as GTA 6’s marketing has done with the “Plays Best on PS5” tagline.

In a follow-up post on social media, Nowakowski insisted The Witcher 4, which is slated for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X and S, remains a multiplatform release, as do all the games CD Projekt has in the works. That presumably means no exclusivity deal for Cyberpunk 2, not that anyone suspected one might be put in place.

“We’re looking forward to our partnership with PlayStation! And just to be clear: The Witcher 4 and our other upcoming titles will remain multiplatform,” Nowakowski said.

Already there is concern around The Witcher 4’s PlayStation marketing deal, following the debate around GTA 6’s “Plays Best on PS5” tagline. As we’ve reported, the Xbox Series X version of Rockstar’s epic has better performance than the PS5 version, which has caused some to say they feel misled.

The Witcher 4 isn’t due out until 2028 so there’s a long time to go before we see the result of CD Projekt’s effort, but marketing is expected to ramp up significantly in the coming months. Excitement is building, and this week CD Projekt said it expects the leap between The Witcher 3 and 4 to be comparable to the one between GTA 5 and 6.

As of October 31, 2026, CD Projekt had 513 staff working on The Witcher 4, which is actually down slightly on the previous number reported three months earlier. The number of people working on Cyberpunk 2, however, has ramped up, from 184 to 199.

CD Projekt has a huge amount going on right now. The Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, launches next year, followed by The Witcher 4 in 2028. CD Projekt has an ambitious plan to release further The Witcher sequels hot on the heels of The Witcher 4 as part of a new trilogy of games. Then there’s Cyberpunk 2 to squeeze in there at some point, The Witcher remake, Project Hadar, and Project Sirius.

items.title: Take-Two Appears to Be Trying to Scrub GTA 6 PC Ports From the Internet, as Vibecoders Race Toward Controversial World First
items.description: Take-Two appears to be taking on the many GTA 6 PC ports currently in the works following Cyberleek’s alleged release of an unauthorized Xbox build of the game.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Take-Two appears to be taking on the many GTA 6 PC ports currently in the works following Cyberleek’s alleged release of an unauthorized Xbox build of the game.

This week, Cyberleek allegedly released the executable file for the incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build they reportedly leaked the week prior, sparking a race within the homebrew scene to port the build to PC. There’s even a website tracking the various attempts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox Series build to PC.

But it looks like Take-Two is taking action, reportedly convincing GitHub to delete an entire network of 3,007 repositories via a DMCA takedown notice.

The takedown we know about relates to ItsNotRexed's GitHub repository and the over 2,900 forks attached to it, which Take-Two said facilitated copyright infringement of GTA 6. Take-Two alleged that the repository Project Leonida repository "exceeds the license Rockstar Games grants to users, constituting copyright infringement.” Here, Take-Two claimed that the repository violated at least Section 2.3 of Rockstar Games’ terms of service:

"The limited license granted in this Agreement does not give you any right to, and you may not, sell, copy, loan, lease, distribute, disassemble, decompile, decrypt, hack, derive source code from, reverse engineer, modify, create derivative works, commercialize, or otherwise exploit the Services (including the Content), Virtual Items, or your Account unless subject to separate, express written terms provided by Rockstar permitting such conduct.”

Additionally, there’s an interesting note in the takedown order that addresses the “bring your own files” defence we’ve seen so often from the homebrew community when it comes to unofficial ports of video games. As you’d expect, Take-Two isn’t in favor of it, insisting that in this case, the files the user must provide come from the unauthorized GTA 6 Xbox build Cyberleek leaked online.

IGN has asked Take-Two for comment.

According to now deleted social media posts, NotRexed, author of the Leonida project, shut it down entirely. There are also screenshots of its Discord showing users posting disclaimers distancing themselves from Project Leonida in case of a federal investigation.

However, many similar projects remain active, risking similar action from Take-Two. Seemingly undeterred, these projects are ongoing, with some getting close to creating a PC port of GTA 6 that is somewhat playable. Some are even streaming their efforts, showing how they are vibecoding a port using agent prompts such as "make no mistakes," "keep finding more stuff and working and pushing," and "work faster."

This is of course a nightmare scenario for Take-Two and Sony and Microsoft, which are benefiting greatly from GTA 6 releasing on console only. The console version of GTA 6 targets 30fps across all platforms, although struggles at times to hit that on base PS5, and Xbox Series X and S. As a result, there is huge interest in a potential PC version offering 60fps gameplay.

As you've probably seen from various viral clips on social media, people are using AI to create clones of popular games and release them on platforms they're not normally available on. We've seen everything from Minecraft playable inside X/Twitter to modders crashing Minecraft and Elden Ring together. Indeed, last month, Rockstar's own Grand Theft Auto 5 was made playable in a browser before it was pulled offline.

Seemingly in response, Anthropic issued an update for Claude that made it harder for people to use the AI model to generate video game clones. In an interview with IGN sister site RPS, former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that Rockstar Games may be keen to port GTA 6 to PC as soon as possible, due to the explosion of AI-generated clones and ports.

Some of this concern has to do with the security of the PS5, with Sony seemingly engaged in a game of Whac-a-Mole with hackers who are trying to jailbreak the latest firmware. If a PS5 jailbreak is made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6 to run, it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and subsequently made available on PC.

Earlier this month, Strauss Zelnick, the boss of Take-Two, responded to the threat of AI-assisted reverse-engineering and decompilation of games in an interview with IGN. He said he was taking the issue seriously, and insisted that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, with all its bells and whistles as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version.

Here’s the exchange:

IGN: We've seen hackers using AI to clone games much faster than ever before, even try to jailbreak consoles. And there is some concern about this leading to potentially GTA 6 being made available on PC unofficially or places that you aren't releasing it. I was just wondering how much of a threat this is to your business? And, is there anything meaningful you can do about it?

Strauss Zelnick: I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business. I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.

IGN: Related, last week Anthropic confirmed they took steps to block Claude from reverse engineering video games. I would assume you would welcome that. And would you like to see other AI companies like OpenAI do the same thing to prevent people from using these powerful AI models to clone your games?

Strauss Zelnick: I think all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's. And if you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected.

During an investor-focused Q&A following the release of Take-Two’s latest financial report, attended by IGN, Zelnick was asked multiple times about the AI reverse-engineering problem. He, again, had strong words in response, suggesting Take-Two was ready to lawyer up.

“This business has been largely immune to piracy concerns forever because of file sizes, complexity of piracy, being connected to servers and the like,” he began. “And undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations.

“That said, it's going to become more of a challenge, as you said, and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.”

Zelnick’s talk about legal activities sparks an obvious question: what can game companies do about AI-assisted reverse engineering? It's a question IGN recently asked when people started to work on a PC port of Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

items.title: Raul Bautista Actor Manny Perez Bought a PS5 So He Could Play GTA 6
items.description: The actor behind one of the best GTA characters of all time has started working his way through GTA 6. Manny Perez, who plays Raul Bautista, bought a PS5 just so he could play.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
The actor behind one of the best GTA characters of all time has started working his way through GTA 6. Manny Perez, who plays Raul Bautista, bought a PS5 just so he could play.

“Guy, I’m playing and this s**t is crazy!” he said in a video posted to social media. “Look how real that looks. I’m learning, I’m loving this, it’s crazy.”

According to Perez, the biggest issue as a non-gamer has been getting used to the DualSense controller, which he called “the stick,” but he’s “getting there.”

The actor sent a follow-up tweet after a fan shared the video. “Will take a while but I will finish this game,” he said. “Thank you all for the support. I’m loving the comments and appreciations.”

Warning! Spoilers for GTA 6 follow.

Raul Batista is a big character in GTA 6 from Chapter 3 onwards, and one of the highlights of the game in terms of performance. Batista steals the show in some really cool scenes, which I won’t spoil, but I can see him becoming a fan favorite as people work their way through the story.

Perez has also been touring Miami and recreating iconic scenes from GTA 6, including his in-car introduction from the Extended Look. Here’s a post showing some of the photos:

It’s kind of killing me how Raul Bautista’s actor (Manny Perez) is already out here touring Miami and recreating scenes from the game LMAO

I love this guy, GOAT @MannyPerez1 https://t.co/KyMhGco8su

— GameRoll (@GameRoll_) November 23, 2026

Perez isn't the only GTA 6 actor who's started to talk about their work on the game and fan reaction to their character. For example, Lexie Shoaibi has spoken out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame after her character, Mandy, went viral online. And Issa Lopez, who plays a radio host on GTA 6’s fictional Cocoteo FM radio station, described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game, calling the project “crazy secretive.”

items.title: GTA 6 Analysis Shows PS5 Version Suffers 'Substantially' More Frequent Frame Rate Drops Than Xbox Series X Version
items.description: The tech experts at Digital Foundry have revealed their analysis of GTA 6, and found the game performs “meaningfully better” on Xbox Series X than the base PS5.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The tech experts at Digital Foundry have revealed their analysis of GTA 6, and found the game performs “meaningfully better” on Xbox Series X than the base PS5.

Sony’s high-profile marketing deal for GTA 6 involved the key phrase, “Plays Best on PS5,” and while that marketing tagline encompasses more than just performance, many are now questioning its validity with GTA 6 out in the wild.

Digital Foundry found that Xbox Series X provides a “virtually identical visual presentation” to the PS5 in terms of overall image clarity and presentation quality, but there is a significant split on performance.

As Rockstar had announced before launch, GTA 6 “targets” 30 frames per second across all platforms, from the Xbox Series S up to the PS5 Pro, but there are moments where the frame rate drops. According to DF’s analysis, the frame rate suffers more on PS5 than Series X.

Here's what DF said on the issue:

PS5 suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops than Series X, which is compounded by the fact that the Xbox machine also benefits from 120Hz VRR support to smooth out minor dips. Ultimately, Series X is meaningfully better off.

Of course, the PS5 Pro version offers the best experience in terms of performance, but it’s interesting to see the Xbox Series X outperform the PS5 here. Some are pointing to non-performance related features, such as the PS5’s haptic feedback, which is great for driving, as playing a role in the phrase “Plays Best on PS5,” and we should be used to marketing speak that is technically not wrong by now. But, as DF reveals, when it comes to performance, there can be no doubting the clear winner.

Indeed, some are calling the “Plays Best on PS5,” phrase “grossly misleading,” claiming that Sony should have said “Plays Best on PS5 Pro” instead.

“I’ve been f***ing fooled,” one person said in the comments of DF’s YouTube video. “They did kind of say in the fine print that ‘best’ referred to the features in the DualSense controller,” another person countered.

“If you are advertising ‘Plays best on X’ to gamers, the immediate thought is going to be ‘Out the two places I can play the game, it is going to play the best on the X console,’” another suggested. “What does ‘Play’ mean to that audience? Performance, stability, possibly higher resolution, less texture pop-in.”

In June, when Sony trumpeted the “Plays Best on PS5” marketing line, it highlighted how GTA 6 takes advantage of the PS5 DualSense controller's haptic feedback and integrated speaker. Sony also highlighted its Tempest 3D AudioTech, which allows you to "surround yourself in the distinct soundscapes of Leonida" through its "highly accurate audio positioning." GTA 6 would also "leverage the PS5's ultra-high speed SSD" to experience GTA 6 "with near-instant load times." Sony's blog post made no mention of performance.

Meanwhile, there are questions around GTA 6’s use of FSR 4.1 on the Xbox Series S version of the game only. Rather than rendering the game at the console's native 1440p, Rockstar used AMD's FSR 4.1 to upscale from 720p to 1080p, which makes GTA 6 one of the first games to use the new upscaling tech on Xbox. It’s thought this tech is what made GTA 6 possible at 30fps on the underpowered Series S in the first place.

Both the Xbox Series X and base PS5 versions of the game instead use Rockstar's in-house TAA (temporal anti-aliasing) solution, and the PS5 Pro uses Sony’s PSSR upscaler. But why not use FSR 4.1 on the Xbox Series X version of GTA 6 also? Similarly, if the PS5 version already supports PSSR, why not use Sony’s AI upscaling model QSSR (Quick Spectral Super Resolution)?

Elsewhere, fans are just marveling at the performance of GTA 6 on Xbox Series S, which — as we’ve reported — shows what Microsoft’s cheaper console is capable of. Ultimately, DF is hoping Rockstar releases GTA 6 updates that improve performance across the board, potentially adding 120Hz VRR support on PlayStation hardware and “stabilising” base console frame rates.

Indeed, some are calling the “Plays Best on PS5,” phrase “grossly misleading,” claiming that Sony should have said “Plays Best on PS5 Pro” instead.

“I’ve been f***ing fooled,” one person said in the comments of DF’s YouTube video. “They did kind of say in the fine print that ‘best’ referred to the features in the DualSense controller,” another person countered.

“If you are advertising ‘Plays best on X’ to gamers, the immediate thought is going to be ‘Out the two places I can play the game, it is going to play the best on the X console,’” another suggested. “What does ‘Play’ mean to that audience? Performance, stability, possibly higher resolution, less texture pop-in.”

In June, when Sony trumpeted the “Plays Best on PS5” marketing line, it highlighted how GTA 6 takes advantage of the PS5 DualSense controller's haptic feedback and integrated speaker. Sony also highlighted its Tempest 3D AudioTech, which allows you to "surround yourself in the distinct soundscapes of Leonida" through its "highly accurate audio positioning." GTA 6 would also "leverage the PS5's ultra-high speed SSD" to experience GTA 6 "with near-instant load times." Sony's blog post made no mention of performance.

Meanwhile, there are questions around GTA 6’s use of FSR 4.1 on the Xbox Series S version of the game only. Rather than rendering the game at the console's native 1440p, Rockstar used AMD's FSR 4.1 to upscale from 720p to 1080p, which makes GTA 6 one of the first games to use the new upscaling tech on Xbox. It’s thought this tech is what made GTA 6 possible at 30fps on the underpowered Series S in the first place.

Both the Xbox Series X and base PS5 versions of the game instead use Rockstar's in-house TAA (temporal anti-aliasing) solution, and the PS5 Pro uses Sony’s PSSR upscaler. But why not use FSR 4.1 on the Xbox Series X version of GTA 6 also? Similarly, if the PS5 version already supports PSSR, why not use Sony’s AI upscaling model QSSR (Quick Spectral Super Resolution)?

Elsewhere, fans are just marveling at the performance of GTA 6 on Xbox Series S, which — as we’ve reported — shows what Microsoft’s cheaper console is capable of. Ultimately, DF is hoping Rockstar releases GTA 6 updates that improve performance across the board, potentially adding 120Hz VRR support on PlayStation hardware and “stabilising” base console frame rates.

items.title: Yes, There Was One Thing Cut from GTA 6 for Australia, NZ
items.description: Rockstar chopped out a temporary stat buff from GTA 6, although players down under may not ever really notice it.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
The Australian version of Grand Theft Auto 6 does differ from the international version in one small way; players down under are not able to use cocaine from their personal inventory to briefly overpower their stamina bar. NZ reportedly has the same version.

In GTA 6, baggies of cocaine can be collected (or skimmed from full bricks) and show up as a consumable on the item wheel in the same section as cigarettes, cigars, and joints. Using one triggers a buff that puts stamina in an overpowered state, albeit only for about 30 seconds. This function was never included in the Australian-specific version of the game, as it would have prevented GTA 6 from being classified in the country until it was removed. Australia’s classification laws allow illicit drug use in games, but using them can’t provide the player with gameplay benefits.

Overpowering your stamina (and everything else) is still possible via the use of adrenaline in the Australian version of GTA 6, and it’s also still possible to drink and smoke whenever you want. The general use of cocaine in story moments also still remains in the Australian version of GTA 6, because these instances aren’t associated with any in-game buffs.

While the caveat that forbids rewards for illicit drug use is bespoke to Australia – and doesn’t apply to NZ – NZ’s rating system (which does piggyback on some Australian and UK classification decisions for unrestricted content) has its own idiosyncrasies. These recently caught out IllFonic’s recent Halloween multiplayer game, which was refused classification in Australia for illicit drug use linked to an incentive or reward (that is, that use of the drug provides a gameplay advantage to the player). Halloween since made its way to NZ, but not Australia. Since this is not Rockstar’s first rodeo, it knew exactly the tweak GTA 6 would require to skirt this continuing quirk in Australian video game ratings and avoid multiple submissions.

GTA 6 arrived late last week, crushing records and becoming the biggest entertainment launch of all time, with retail sales soaring to $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours. In my review for IGN I called it “the single most impressive video game I have ever played,” a sentiment shared by developers similarly stunned by how radically advanced it is.
